name: signatures
headline: One kind of name: the *signature*
sub: Sixty-four characters, computed from the bytes themselves. Same content → same name, on every machine, forever.
say: Everything in Hypercomb has one kind of name: a signature — the SHA-256 hash of its content. Sixty-four characters that are the same on every machine, in every country, forever. Same content, same signature; change one byte and it's a different thing with a different name. This single idea does enormous work. Content can be verified — the name proves the bytes. It deduplicates itself — the same picture stored twice is stored once. It can be cached forever — a signature never goes stale. And it can be shared as a tiny string that any participant can resolve. Signatures aren't an implementation detail. They are the identity system, the reference system, and the trust system — all at once.
